newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Sporadic shelling in Mogadishu, families flee.
newsitem.headline: Sporadic shelling in Mogadishu, families flee.

text.p: Sporadic mortar fire on parts of southern Mogadishu punctuated a lull on Thursday after six days of battles between rival factions killed more than 135 people.
Witnesses said dozens of families used the relative calm on Thursday to flee their homes for safer parts of the capital.
One woman was killed when a mortar bomb hit a building near a junction held by forces loyal to faction chief Hussein Aideed.
Reasons for the lull were unclear. But some residents feared more fighting was inevitable and said both sides were probably preparing for new battles or had run short of ammunition.

Fighting since last Friday has pitted Aideed's militiamen against forces of his rivals -- Hassan Ali Osman Atto in south Mogadishu, Ali Mahdi Mohamed in north Mogadishu and Moslem fundamentalist leader Musa Sudi Yalahow in Medina district.
More than 135 people have been killed and 900 wounded since last Friday and aid workers said they feared the death toll was closer to 300. Thousands of civilians have fled their homes.

Hussein Aideed, a 34-year-old former U.S. marine, succeeded his father Mohamed Farah Aideed on his death in August. He was elected president of Somalia by his supporters but both he and his government are rejected by most other faction leaders.
